rationale: This is the third mechanical aggregation of two already-tested gates (product t=5.23, MIN t=5.13) and is a cosmetic combinator swap rather than a substantively different mechanism; the hypothesis also contradicts the earlier claim that the two gates measure economically independent defects, so a small Sharpe change either way will not be interpretable.

A clean one-variable ablation that isolates whether the dlc obligation term contributes anything beyond cash+flow resources, but it sits between two already-strong tested specs (cash-only t=5.49, full cushion t=5.23) so the informational payoff is diagnostic and modest rather than novel.

Replacing the cross-sectional cash-holdings level with a within-firm five-year TS_RANK is a genuine economic distinction (accumulation vs. level, and it sidesteps the industry-composition critique), though the 5-point TS_RANK is coarse and the leg is a close cousin of change-in-cash measures already documented in the literature.

This is the only proposal that tests *why* the cash gate works, and the sign prediction on profitability volatility is internally consistent with the precautionary-value story and falsifiable in a way that distinguishes it from the failed unconditional stability screen; the main risk is that a triple rank product will load on small/high-vol firms and confound with the known idiosyncratic-volatility effect.

The stock-versus-flow complementarity is a reasonable refinement of the strongest gate and the MIN structure is defensible, but the flow leg is close to the already-tested cash-return gates and the COALESCE fallback to accrual profitability partly defeats the stated "not burning cash" interpretation.

A legitimate and cheap parsimony ablation of the R&D addback against a gate that shares no accounting-mismeasurement theme with it, though with xrd coalesced to zero for most firms the numerator difference is small and a null result is the most likely and least informative outcome.
